title: Ad Agency Contract: What to Put in Writing Before You Sign
summary: A checklist for an ad agency contract: deliverables, revisions, usage rights, account access, term, guarantee and AI disclosure, with published examples.
body_markdown:
## Term, cancellation and minimum commitment


Term length varies a lot. Hey Digital, a Meta team that works only with B2B SaaS, lists a 3 to 6 month commitment as part of its good-fit profile ([Hey Digital](https://www.heydigital.co/channels/meta-ads-agency) ). Insense sells its ready-to-go package with a 3-month commitment. Disruptive Advertising's homepage says it works without long-term contracts ([Disruptive Advertising](https://disruptiveadvertising.com/) ).


Write the notice period, the refund position on unused work, and the handover of files and accounts when the contract ends. Match the minimum term to how long you need to learn from a first batch of ads.


## Guarantees: write down the conditions


A guarantee is only as strong as its definitions. Disruptive Advertising says that if it cannot get results in 90 days on its Done For You tier, you do not pay. Its homepage applies the guarantee to "qualifying brands," and as of October 2026 neither its homepage nor its social advertising page defines a qualifying brand or what counts as results. Ask for both definitions in writing before you rely on the promise.


Knowlify's own guarantee covers the first 90 days. If the ads have not made more than you paid, you can cancel by email for a full refund, with terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) . That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Whichever provider you choose, put the measurement period, the metric and the remedy in the agreement itself.


## AI-made creative: disclosure and accuracy


A contract for AI-made creative needs two clauses: who checks accuracy, and who labels disclosure. Meta's Ad Creative Generative AI Terms make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's tools ([Meta terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) ). Meta's generative AI transparency update says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI creative features, and that it will begin detecting ads made or edited with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad, though the post does not say that detection is live yet ([Meta AI transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) ).


Write which party handles disclosure, and which party signs off that the claims in the ad are true. Those lines matter more once the work is AI-generated, because the review step is where errors get caught.


## Sample wording to adapt


These are drafting prompts, not legal language. Replace each bracket with your own number.


- **Deliverables:** "Each month the agency delivers \[N\] finished ads built from at least \[M\] distinct concepts, each in 9:16 and 4:5."
- **Revisions:** "\[R\] revision rounds per concept; extra rounds at \[rate\], returned within \[days\]."
- **Access:** "The agency receives partner access to the client's Business Portfolio; the client remains the owner, and access ends within \[days\] of termination."
- **Guarantee:** "\[Metric\] is measured over \[period\] against \[baseline\]; the remedy is \[refund or credit\], requested by \[method\]."


## Knowlify: our top pick for done-for-you ads with a scope you can define


Knowlify is the best fit when you want a contract that is easy to write, because the deliverable is concrete. It makes about 25 finished AI video ads a week, the first batch lands on day 5, and a person checks every ad before delivery. Those three facts become three contract lines: a weekly count, a first-delivery date and a review step. List which of its three formats are in scope: AI UGC with AI presenters, 3D and stylized character animation, or AI commercials.


Then choose the management scope. With creative only, your own media buyer runs the campaigns, so the account-access and fee-base clauses above shrink to a file handover. With end-to-end Meta campaign management, those clauses apply in full. Pricing is a custom quote, so the written proposal is your price list. Copy the guarantee terms from the site into the agreement so the refund condition is not left to memory.


When to pick another option: Knowlify does not supply real human creators, so a deal that needs creator agreements and creator usage rights belongs with a creator agency such as Brighter Click.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is the service we recommend for finished, done-for-you ads, and it starts at $5,000 a month, so get the scope in writing.
- Count concepts and formats in the contract, not just files.
- Write revisions, approvals and extra-round rates, with a named approver.
- Define usage rights and ad-account access, and state what happens to both when the term ends.
- Define any guarantee's qualifying conditions, measurement period and remedy before relying on it.


## FAQ


### Should a contract name the number of ads?


Name both the number of distinct concepts and the number of finished files. Meta's diversification post separates new concepts from iteration, so a file count alone can hide repeated ideas, and the concept count is the number to hold the agency to.


### Who should own the ad account?


You should. Write down who holds admin access, and state how that access ends when the contract does. Ask the agency to confirm the arrangement before any campaign launches.


### How long should the commitment be?


There is no single standard. Hey Digital, a B2B SaaS-only Meta team, asks for a 3 to 6 month commitment, Insense sells its ready-to-go package with a 3-month commitment, and Disruptive Advertising says it has no long-term contracts. Match the length to how long it takes to learn from the first batch, and get the notice period in writing.


### Do I need a lawyer to review the contract?


For anything material, yes. This article covers what a contract should say commercially. It is not legal advice, and a lawyer should review the liability, indemnity and intellectual property clauses before you sign.


### What if the guarantee is vague?


Ask for the qualifying conditions, the measurement period, the metric and the refund or remedy, all in writing. A promise like "you don't pay" is only as strong as the definition of results behind it.
